input.text:
Let TypedDict items declare default values, so that a missing NotRequired key has a known
value when read, and type checkers can treat d["key"] as always present.

rejected_ideas.idea: Misalignment with how unions apply to values
rejected_ideas.section: Rejected Ideas / Marking absence of a value with a special constant / Misalignment with how unions apply to values
rejected_ideas.summary: However this use of ...|Missing, equivalent to Union[..., Missing], doesn’t align well with what a union normally means: Union[...] always describes the type of a value that is present. By contrast missingness or non-totality is a property of a variable instead.

rejected_ideas.idea: Support a New Syntax of Specifying Keys
rejected_ideas.section: Rejected Ideas / Support a New Syntax of Specifying Keys
rejected_ideas.summary: By introducing a new syntax that allows specifying string keys, we could deprecate the functional syntax of defining TypedDict types and address the key conflict issues if we decide to reserve a special key to type extra items.
rejected_ideas.reason: While such users have a way to get around the issue, it's still a problem for them if they upgrade Python (or typing-extensions).

rejected_ideas.section: Rejected Ideas / Support Extra Items with Intersection
rejected_ideas.summary: Supporting intersections in Python's type system requires a lot of careful consideration, and it can take a long time for the community to reach a consensus on a reasonable design.
